Policy rule R1: Verify before you block on a weak signal: R1. Verify before you block on a weak signal. If the case rests on a single signal (including a risk score alone) and your assessed fraud probability is below 0.70, recommend `VERIFY_WITH_CUSTOMER` or `STEP_UP_AUTH` before any block. Blocking a legitimate customer on one signal is a policy breach.

Policy rule R6: Shared origin: R6. Shared origin. When several cards show fraud from the same device profile, the same billing region, or the same recipient email in one window, name the shared element, recommend `CREATE_CASE` and `FILE_REPORT`, and `MONITOR_CONNECTED_CARDS` for every card that shares it.

sar.narrative: Between 2016-12-29 and 2016-12-31, card C00782-K1 belonging to customer C00782 was used for 2 transaction(s) totalling $959.27, of which the transaction that triggered this investigation was $934.98 on 2016-12-29, and the activity was conducted in person under product code W, billed in region 327.0. Cardholder denies the transaction on contact, and on contact cardholder states they did not make the transaction and still holds the card, though that response is an assumption recorded in the case file, as no cardholder replies were available to this investigation. On this transaction, 2 of the card-detail match flags M1-M9 came back F, and the bank has 1 confirmed-fraud case(s) already closed on this card (CC-3048), pattern(s): card_not_present_new_device, while the bank's closed investigations also record 1 confirmed fraud case(s) on this card (CC-3579, CC-3048). The same device profile was used by 1 other card(s) in the thirty days to 2016-12-29 (C13355-K1), indicating a common actor operating across more than one cardholder, and connected components over the device-sharing graph place this card in a bounded component of 2 cards (C13355-K1), linked transitively through device profiles each used by no more than 8 cards. The activity is suspicious because it is consistent with mixed-channel activity consistent with stolen credentials, assessed at a 94% probability of being fraudulent on 4 independent pieces of evidence drawn from the transaction graph and the institution's closed-case history, and because $934.98 is 12.7x this card's median and above its 95th percentile, though large outliers appear on 16% of cleared alarms and 6% of confirmed fraud. The filing is made because the activity connects to a device profile shared with other compromised cards, which requires a report regardless of amount, and because the 5 closed cases whose transaction most resembles this one (CC-5502, CC-1192, CC-4870, CC-3722, CC-4562) closed as 5 confirmed fraud (account takeover, out of region use) and 0 cleared. External email-domain intelligence classifies 'gmail.com' as a free webmail address, which is the baseline, and the activity is also suspicious because the 2 of the card-detail match flags M1-M9 came back F, which is 2.9x more likely on confirmed fraud than on a cleared alarm (22.7% vs 7.9%), prompting the institution to block the card and schedule it for reissue, open an internal investigation case, place the card under heightened monitoring, and place the cards sharing the same origin under monitoring.
